history.summary: The Aksharwadi Temple is the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir of Bhavnagar, located in the Aksharwadi locality on Waghawadi Road. Opened in 2006, it was constructed by the BAPS Shri Seva Sansthan under the inspiration of Pramukh Swami Maharaj (per devotee accounts - verify official attribution). Built in traditional Hindu style following the Shilpa Shastras, the two-storey temple has three domes, 97 intricately carved pillars, 17 ornate domes, 220 stone beams, 57 stone screens, 3 porticos and 256 statues of spiritual personalities, with terracotta work, wall paintings, a cradle of Lord Krishna and surrounding gardens. The middle shrine holds Gopinathji Maharaj and Harikrishna Maharaj; the western side holds Dharmadev, Bhakti Mata and Vasudevanarayan; the eastern side holds Revti-Baldevji, Krishna and Suryanarayan. It serves as the main Swaminarayan spiritual and cultural hub of Bhavnagar, with a large garden campus. Coordinates (21.754075, 72.141858) from the official BAPS mandir listing page.

town_description: Bhavnagar is a major port city and former princely state capital in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, on the western shore of the Gulf of Khambhat. Founded in 1724 by Bhavsinhji Gohil, it is known for the Takhteshwar Temple hill, Nilambag Palace, Gaurishankar Lake and the nearby sea temples of Koliyak and Talaja, as well as the Blackbuck National Park at Velavadar. It is well connected by rail, road and a domestic airport.

travel.railway: Bhavnagar Terminus, approx. 4 km on Waghawadi Road.
travel.road: On Waghawadi Road in the Aksharwadi locality of Bhavnagar city, approx. 4 km from the railway station; reachable by auto-rickshaw, taxi and city buses.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Sunday evening Ravi Sabha is a good time for a devotional visit.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported intervals approx. 7:30 AM-10:15 AM, 11:15 AM-12:00 noon, 4:00-6:00 PM, 7:00-8:15 PM daily, with midday closures (verify - hours vary by season and festival). Entry is free (verify). Modest dress and shoe removal required as with all BAPS mandirs.
